saved_nonempty_lines.complete_saved_text: Mina and Reijo can help bring a local investigation to an effective conclusion while remaining opposed over culpability and repair. Their encounter starts with accusation, challenged certainty and an actual confrontation. Shared inquiry and capture change what they can do together. They do not produce an identical account of the original wrong or the adequacy of apology. Mina later concedes that deciding guilt was wrong, but defers the institutional apology; Reijo calls that insufficient. After Kisaki's actual official apology, Mina minimizes the mistake and Reijo still expresses dissatisfaction while respecting Rumi's decision for the day. The relationship has therefore changed through practical action without acquiring complete reconciliation. [A01 L103–109/L129–149; BA:event:826:006:u0016–0031; 007; 010–012.]
